issues.description: No coded analysis data are included and the document provides no path, format, delivery route, or exact usable-sample file for the 135-auditor experiment. A deidentified author-prepared dataset is the primary route; current access and field coverage remain unknown. The reported firm confidentiality term does not establish that the required data are blocked.

The PDF claims raw-to-final code is included, but its embedded Stata blocks do not load/import data or calculate dv5/trust3; their definitions are supplied, so they may already exist in the coded input. The SEM path consumes testing, which is not defined elsewhere in the datasheet. The exact author-prepared columns and any missing construction steps remain unknown.

Substantive Stata analysis code is embedded in a PDF rather than supplied as a standalone driver. It requires extraction/reflow into a separate working copy and a prepared Stata dataset already in memory; the PDF itself is not a directly executable entry file.

The embedded Stata 17 Table 1 and Table 2 commands use stat(n dv5) and stat(n trust3). The checked version-specific material confirms table's stat() syntax but did not establish whether n is accepted as an alias for the nonmissing-value count in the new table command; retain this exact syntax question for Stata 17/18 help or author clarification without changing the estimator or statistics.

evidence.description: Author datasheet title; it matches the frozen output header title.
evidence.quote: How Does Management Voluntary Disclosure Behavior Influence Auditors’ Judgments?

evidence.description: The datasheet describes experimental data collection, 135 auditors, manual Excel coding, and statistical analyses.
evidence.quote:
See the article for a detailed description of the procedures used to generate the data. Data reported
in this manuscript were mostly collected in-person in May and June 2019 at an accounting firm
training event using paper and pencil. In order anonymize the data, we collected additional data
online using the Qualtrics platform in October 2019 from participants at a second firm, whom we
identified through our professional contacts. Total participants were 135 auditors from two Big 4
firms. Both authors assisted in data collection process. Kamber Vittori manually coded the raw
data from the May 2019 collection into Excel and Sean Hillison coded the June 2019 collection.
Both authors and a research assistant reviewed the coding and raw data. Both authors conducted
the statistical analyses in SPSS and Stata.

evidence.description: The authors say the data were not proprietary, while one firm required identity confidentiality; this does not establish an access barrier for deidentified analysis data.
evidence.quote:
Item 3. Proprietary Nature of Data
Our data was not obtained on a proprietary basis; however one participating firm required a written
confidentiality agreement that protected the identity of the firm that provided the majority of the
participants. With permission of the firm, we have provided the editors with contact information
for a representative of the firm under separate cover.

evidence.description: The datasheet says raw-to-final and primary analysis code is at the end; the supplied content actually contains only embedded Stata analysis/indicator statements.
evidence.quote:
Item 5. Code Used to Conduct Primary Analyses
The code to convert the raw data into the final dataset and conduct the primary analyses is available
at the end of this document. As the data were obtained using an experiment, identifiers (e.g., CIK,
CUSIP, etc.) are not applicable.

evidence.description: The author definitions for the disclosure and optimism condition fields.
evidence.quote:
disclosure: indicator variable for our disclosure conditions; 0 for no disclosure, 1 for voluntary
disclosure, and 2 for mandated disclosure

optimism: indicator variable for our forecast optimism conditions; 0 for lower optimism, 1 for
higher optimism

evidence.description: The author defines dv5 as a reverse-coded average of five skeptical-belief measures.
evidence.quote:
dv5: simple average of five measures of skeptical beliefs, each reverse-coded for presentation
purposes so that higher values represent more skepticism

evidence.description: The five skeptical-belief questionnaire measures underlying dv5.
evidence.quote:
• reasonable: How reasonable are the revenue projections from 2019 – 2023 used in the
       discounted cash flow analysis? 1 = “Not Reasonable” to 7 = “Very Reasonable”
   • persuasive: How persuasive is the information provided by the CFO in the memo to
       support projected revenue from 2019 – 2023? 1 = “Not Persuasive” to 7 = “Very
       Persuasive”
   • strength: How would you rate the strength of the audit evidence provided by management
       in the memo to support projected revenue from 2019 – 2023? 1 = “Weak Evidence” to 7
       = “Strong Evidence”
   • justifiable: How would you rate the justifiability of the audit evidence provided by
       management in the memo to support projected revenue from 2019 – 2023 to accounting
       firm regulators (e.g., PCAOB inspectors)? 1 = “Not at all Justifiable” to 7 = “Extremely
       Justifiable”
   • conclude: To what extent are you prepared to conclude that the revenue projections from
       2019 – 2023 are reasonable? 1 = “Not at All Prepared to Conclude” to 7 = “Completely
       Prepared to Conclude”

evidence.description: The author defines trust3 as the average of three trustworthiness measures.
evidence.quote:
trust3: simple average of three measures of management trustworthiness, each coded so that
higher values represent higher assessed trustworthiness
    • trust: How much trust do you have in the information provided by the CFO to support
        projected revenue from 2019 – 2023? 1 = “No Trust” to 7 = “High Trust”
    • trustworthy: I believe that Smith management is very trustworthy. 1 = “Strongly
        Disagree” to 7 = “Strongly Agree”
    • honest: I believe that Smith management is very honest. 1 = “Strongly Disagree” to 7 =
        “Strongly Agree”

evidence.description: The first reported analysis uses Stata 17 and supplies Table 1 descriptives and a two-factor ANOVA.
evidence.quote:
We first conducted a 3x2 ANOVA model to examine the effects of our independent variables
(disclosure and forecast optimism) on our dependent variable (dv5). The following syntax
generated results reported in the article (analyses conducted using Stata 17):

Table 1: Auditors’ Skeptical Beliefs about Forward-Looking Information

Panel A: Descriptive Statistics for Auditors’ Skeptical Beliefs about Forward-Looking
Information

table optimism disclosure, stat(mean dv5) stat(sd dv5) stat(n dv5)

Panel B: ANOVA Model

anova dv5 disclosure##optimism

evidence.description: The supplied Table 1 simple-effect contrasts, margins, and pairwise tests.
evidence.quote:
Panel C: Simple Effect Comparisons

contrast r.disclosure@optimism
contrast a.disclosure@optimism
contrast r.optimism@disclosure
margins, at(disclosure=1 optimism=1) at(disclosure=2 optimism=1) at(disclosure=0
optimism=1) at(disclosure=1 optimism=0) at(disclosure=2 optimism=0) at(disclosure=0
optimism=0) post
test _b[4._at]=_b[5._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F)) " p = " ttail(r(df_r), sqrt(r(F)))
test _b[4._at]=_b[6._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F)) " p = " ttail(r(df_r), sqrt(r(F)))
test _b[5._at]=_b[6._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F))
test _b[2._at]=_b[5._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F)) " p = " ttail(r(df_r), sqrt(r(F)))
test _b[3._at]=_b[6._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F)) " p = " ttail(r(df_r), sqrt(r(F)))
test _b[1._at]=_b[4._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F))
test _b[1._at]=_b[2._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F))
test _b[1._at]=_b[3._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F))
test _b[2._at]=_b[3._at]
display "t = " sqrt(r(F))

evidence.description: The datasheet maps the mediation analysis to Table 2 and Figure 2; the Figure 2 label has no separate diagram in the PDF.
evidence.quote:
We also tested a multicategorial mediation path model to examine whether the effects of our
independent variables on our dependent variable occur through perceptions of management
trustworthiness (trust3). The following syntax generated results reported in the article (analyses
conducted using Stata 17):

Table 2: Auditors’ Perceptions of Management Trustworthiness

table optimism disclosure, stat(mean trust3) stat(sd trust3) stat(n trust3)

Figure 2: Mediation Path Model

evidence.description: The supplied Stata code creates no and mand from disclosure.
evidence.quote:
Indicator variable generation for path model
    • no = 1 for no disclosure; 0 for voluntary or mandated
    • mand = 1 for mandated; 0 for voluntary or no disclosure

gen no = 1 if disclosure==0
replace no = 0 if disclosure==1 | disclosure==2
gen mand = 1 if disclosure==2
replace mand = 0 if disclosure==1 | disclosure==0

evidence.description: The embedded SEM program uses trust3 and dv5 and references an otherwise undefined observed variable, testing.
evidence.quote:
Mediation Model Testing
program bootind, rclass
sem(0:trust3 <- no mand)(0:dv5 <- trust3@b1 no mand)(1:trust3 <- no mand)(1:dv5 <-
trust3@b1 no mand)(testing <- dv5@b2), group(optimism) nocapslatent variance(0:e.trust3@v1
e.dv5@v2 e.testing@v3) variance(1:e.trust3@v1 e.dv5@v2 e.testing@v3)

evidence.description: The SEM program returns four indirect-effect scalars, bootstraps them with 5,000 replications at 90%, then requests percentile and bias-corrected intervals.
